headline: A personalized cancer vaccine passes its biggest test

sources.title: Moderna and Merck say mRNA cancer vaccine succeeded in late-stage melanoma trial (STAT News)
Moderna, Merck unveil mRNA-based cancer vaccine that cuts spread (Al Jazeera)
Cancer breakthrough as personalised mRNA vaccine stops melanoma returning (Gavi VaccinesWork)
Moderna reaches 'landmark moment' in melanoma vaccine trial (video, CBS News)

chunks.text: For years, scientists have dreamed of a [[vaccine]] against cancer. This week, that dream took a giant step forward. Drug companies Moderna and Merck, which {{teamed up}} years ago, announced that their [[personalized]] [[melanoma]] vaccine passed its biggest test yet. The news {{came out}} on August 19, and doctors around the world are calling it a possible [[turning point]]. It is the first time a vaccine of this kind has succeeded in a large, final-stage [[trial]].

verbs.why: Team up means two people or companies join forces to work on something together. Moderna and Merck teamed up years before this vaccine succeeded.

verbs.correct: To be published for the public
verbs.wrong: To be kept secret for years
verbs.why: Come out means information becomes public, like news, a report, or a movie. Here it is the announcement that a vaccine trial finally succeeded.

chunks.text: Here is how it works. First, [[surgeons]] {{cut out}} the patient's [[tumor]] and send a piece to a [[laboratory]]. Scientists read the cancer's [[genetic code]] and {{pick out}} up to 34 tiny changes, called [[mutations]], that are most likely to alert the body's defenses. Next, a personal [[dose]] is {{put together}} piece by piece for that one patient and nobody else. The shot trains the [[immune system]] to {{hunt down}} escaped cancer cells the way police chase a runaway prisoner.

verbs.why: Cut out means to remove a part by cutting it away, literally with scissors or, as here, a surgeon's knife. Surgeons cut out the tumor before scientists study it.

verbs.correct: To choose from a larger group
verbs.why: Pick out means to choose specific items from a larger group, like the riskiest changes in a tumor's genetic code. It is a careful, deliberate choice, not a random one.
Put together means to build something whole from separate pieces. Each vaccine dose is put together from mutations unique to that one patient.
Hunt down means to keep searching until you find your target. The immune system hunts down cancer cells that escaped the original tumor.

chunks.text: The numbers behind the announcement are strong. More than 1,000 patients with serious melanoma joined the [[Phase 3]] trial after surgery. Patients who received the vaccine together with Keytruda, a famous cancer [[drug]], stayed [[cancer-free]] longer than patients who got the drug alone. For many of them, the melanoma has not {{come back}} at all. The [[combination]] also {{slowed down}} the disease's spread to other [[organs]]. An earlier, smaller study had already cut the risk of return in half. [[Investors]] noticed too: Moderna's [[stock price]] {{shot up}} within hours of the announcement.

verbs.why: Here come back means a disease returns after treatment seemed to work. For many patients in this trial, the melanoma has not come back at all.
Slow down here means to make something else move or spread less quickly. The drug combination slowed down how fast the cancer spread to other organs.
Shoot up means to rise very quickly and sharply, often about numbers or prices. Moderna's stock price shot up within hours of the announcement.

chunks.text: What happens next? The companies are already talking with [[regulators]], and independent [[experts]] will {{go over}} the full numbers line by line at a coming medical meeting. Nobody knows yet how long the [[protection]] lasts. But if everything holds, the companies hope to {{roll out}} the treatment to thousands of patients as early as next year. And researchers are ready to {{take on}} the next challenge: using the same method against lung, kidney, and [[pancreatic]] cancer. One cancer expert said it best: this is where things begin.

verbs.why: Go over means to examine something closely, point by point, before trusting it. Experts will go over the full trial results at a medical meeting.

verbs.correct: To make available to many people
verbs.wrong: To test on a small group first
verbs.why: Roll out means to gradually make something available to many people, like a new treatment. Companies hope to roll out the vaccine to thousands of patients next year.

verbs.wrong: To avoid a hard task politely
verbs.why: Take on means to accept a hard challenge and commit to it. Researchers hope to take on other cancers next, using the same method.

mainIdea.s: A personalized cancer vaccine passed a large final-stage trial for the first time, keeping melanoma from returning in many patients. The treatment could reach patients next year.
mainIdea.why: The vaccine, built for each patient and given with Keytruda, kept people cancer-free longer and slowed the disease's spread.

mainIdea.s: A new cancer vaccine protects healthy people from ever developing melanoma, like a flu shot. Doctors will soon offer it to everyone who spends too much time in the sun.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the vaccine treats patients who already had melanoma removed. It is not a shot for healthy people.

mainIdea.s: Regulators quietly approved a cheap new pill this week that cures every type of skin cancer within a month. Hospitals say the demand is already far bigger than the supply.
mainIdea.why: There is no pill and no approval yet. The vaccine passed a trial, and talks with regulators have just started.

tf.s: Each dose of the vaccine is put together for one single patient
tf.why: Scientists read the tumor's genetic code and pick out up to 34 mutations for that patient's shot.

tf.s: The vaccine was designed to work alone, without any other drug
tf.why: It was tested together with Keytruda, and the combination beat the drug alone.

tf.s: In the trial, patients who got the vaccine stayed cancer-free longer
tf.why: The melanoma also spread less, and for many patients it has not come back at all.

tf.s: The companies plan to wait ten years before offering the treatment
tf.why: They hope to roll it out to thousands of patients as early as next year.

tf.s: Doctors already know exactly how long the protection lasts
tf.why: That is still unknown. Experts will go over the full numbers at a coming medical meeting.

tf.s: Researchers want to take on other cancers with the same method
tf.why: Lung, kidney, and pancreatic cancer are next on the list.
